regime.headline: Hawkish repricing
regime.paragraph: Rates markets priced a more hawkish policy path: US Treasury yields 2Y +18bp to 4.75% and 10Y +11bp to 5.00%. The US curve saw a bear flattener in 2s10s (-7bp to 25bp). The dollar rose 0.7%, gold fell 1.1%, the S&P 500 rose 1.3% and Brent rose 0.5%. US high-yield spreads tightened 8bp. The standout move was US 1Y Treasury (+18bp, 3.8x its 20-day volatility).

regions.name: United States
regions.text: Treasuries sold off with the front end leading, 2Y +18bp to 4.75% and 10Y +11bp to 5.00%: a bear flattener (2s10s -7bp). Markets added 8bp of Fed tightening over 12 months (now +90bp). The dollar rose 0.7% and the S&P 500 rose 1.3%.

regions.name: United Kingdom
regions.text: Gilts sold off with the front end leading, 2Y +2bp to 4.89% and 10Y -1bp to 5.22%: a twist flattener (2s10s -2bp). Gilts outperformed Treasuries by 12bp at 10Y. Markets added 16bp of BoE tightening over 12 months (now +86bp). Sterling fell 0.5% and the FTSE 100 rose 0.8%.

regions.name: Europe
regions.text: Bunds sold off with the front end leading, 2Y +4bp to 3.12% and 10Y +2bp to 3.32%: a bear flattener (2s10s -2bp). BTP-Bund tightened 5bp to 102bp. Markets added 9bp of ECB tightening over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy (now +64bp). The euro fell 0.7% and the Euro Stoxx 50 rose 1.0%.

regions.name: Japan
regions.text: JGB 10Y yields rose 10bp to 2.785%, with 30Y +7bp. The yen weakened as USD/JPY moved +0.7% to 159.78. Markets added 9bp of BoJ tightening over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy (now +93bp). The Nikkei fell 0.7%.

regions.name: China

relationships.statement: Higher US yields supported the dollar.
relationships.lesson: Higher US yields raise the return on dollar assets and attract capital. When the dollar moves against yields, risk sentiment or non-US news is usually driving FX instead.

relationships.statement: Front-end-led selling flattened the Treasury curve: markets priced a more hawkish Fed.
relationships.lesson: Front-end yields rose more than the long end: the market is pricing a more hawkish central bank.

relationships.statement: Credit confirmed the equity rally as high-yield spreads tightened.
relationships.lesson: Equities and credit both price corporate risk. When they disagree, credit (the more senior claim) is often the better signal.
Gold pays no coupon, so higher real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding it. A break often reflects central-bank buying, geopolitical hedging or dollar moves.

relationships.statement: Tighter BTP–Bund spreads signalled stronger demand for periphery risk.
relationships.lesson: BTP–Bund is the euro area's main gauge of sovereign and fragmentation risk; it usually widens with risk-off and narrows when risk appetite is strong.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the Bank of England, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 4.00%. Markets price a 68% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 3.5 hikes (86bp) over 12 months; terminal 4.88%. The 12-month pricing moved +16bp on the day. Method: Bank of England SONIA OIS curve. Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +86bp is 3.5 moves.

interview.question: Why did the dollar strengthen?
interview.answer: DXY moved +0.7% alongside a +11bp move in 10Y Treasuries and -4bp in the US–Germany 2Y spread. The textbook link is relative rates: higher US yields versus the rest of the world raise the carry on USD.

interview.question: Was today's Treasury sell-off driven by real yields or inflation expectations?
interview.answer: Nominal yields rose 11.5bp, driven by real yields (real +3.0bp, breakeven -2.0bp). Nominal yield = real yield + breakeven inflation. Real-yield-led moves usually reflect policy expectations or growth; breakeven-led moves reflect inflation risk, often energy prices. Brent moved +0.5%.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the European Central Bank, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 2.50%. Markets price a 95% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 2.6 hikes (64bp) over 12 months; terminal 3.22%. The 12-month pricing moved +9bp on the day. Method: Government bill-curve proxy (indicative). Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +64bp is 2.6 moves.

interview.question: Why did Bunds outperform JGBs?
interview.answer: 10Y JGBs moved +10bp versus +2bp for Bunds, so the spread moved +8bp to -54bp (54th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.
